title: Life of Antony (Ἀντώνιος)
author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Plutarch. Life of Antony. c. 100-110 CE. Loeb Classical Library, Vol. IX.
notes: Primary narrative source written ~130 years after Antony's death. Draws on lost earlier sources and incorporates anti-Antonian Augustan propaganda. Downgraded from A: secondary narrative with known bias.

title: Civil Wars, Books 2-5 (Ῥωμαϊκά)
author: Appian of Alexandria
citation_detail: Appian. Civil Wars, Books 2-5. c. 150-160 CE. Loeb Classical Library, Vols. III-IV.
notes: Detailed narrative of civil wars from Gracchi to Actium. Books 3-5 cover the Second Triumvirate. Draws on sources hostile to Antony. Downgraded from A: secondary narrative with hostile bias.

title: Roman History, Books 41-51 (Ῥωμαϊκὴ Ἱστορία)
author: Cassius Dio
citation_detail: Cassius Dio. Roman History, Books 41-51. c. 210-230 CE. Loeb Classical Library, Vols. IV-V.
notes: Most complete continuous narrative of the period. Heavily influenced by Augustan tradition. Downgraded from A: late secondary source with Augustan bias.

title: Philippics (Philippicae)
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
citation_detail: Cicero. Philippics. 44-43 BCE. Loeb Classical Library, Nos. 189, 507.
notes: Fourteen speeches against Antony. Contemporary but deeply hostile — Cicero was Antony's political enemy. Downgraded from A: partisan contemporary source.

title: Civil War (Commentarii de Bello Civili)
author: Gaius Julius Caesar
citation_detail: Caesar. Civil War (Commentarii de Bello Civili). c. 48-47 BCE. Loeb Classical Library, No. 39.
notes: First-person account of civil war 49-48 BCE. Contemporary but self-serving propaganda. Downgraded from A: partisan contemporary source.

title: Life of Augustus (Divus Augustus)
author: Suetonius
citation_detail: Suetonius. Life of Augustus (Divus Augustus). c. 119-121 CE. Loeb Classical Library, No. 31.
notes: Biography of Augustus covering the conflict with Antony. Draws on Augustan-era sources including Augustus' own memoirs. Downgraded from A: secondary with pro-Augustan bias.

title: Res Gestae Divi Augusti
author: Augustus
citation_detail: Augustus. Res Gestae Divi Augusti. c. 14 CE. Loeb Classical Library, No. 152.
notes: Augustus' first-person funerary inscription. Contemporary but self-serving propaganda. Downgraded from A: partisan contemporary source.

title: Triumviral coinage and inscriptions (RRC 489-545)
author: Various
citation_detail: Crawford, M. Roman Republican Coinage (RRC) 489-545. 43-30 BCE.
notes: Coins issued by Antony and triumvirs provide contemporary visual evidence. Includes legionary denarii (32-31 BCE) and Cleopatra portrait coins. Downgraded from A: material evidence but limited textual content.

title: Plutarch: Life of Antony (Cambridge Greek and Latin Classics)
author: C.B.R. Pelling
citation_detail: Pelling, C.B.R. Plutarch: Life of Antony. Cambridge Greek and Latin Classics. Cambridge University Press, 1988.
notes: Definitive modern commentary on Plutarch's Life of Antony. Critical analysis of Plutarch's sources, biases, and historical accuracy.

title: Antony and Cleopatra
author: Adrian Goldsworthy
citation_detail: Goldsworthy, Adrian. Antony and Cleopatra. Weidenfeld & Nicolson, 2010.
notes: Modern scholarly biography combining literary sources, archaeology, and military history. Strives to separate Augustan propaganda from historical fact.

title: The Roman Revolution
author: Ronald Syme
citation_detail: Syme, Ronald. The Roman Revolution. Oxford University Press, 1939.
notes: Foundational study of the transition from Republic to Principate. Influential analysis of Antony as a Caesarian leader. Classic but Augustan-skeptical perspective.
